1. Charitable Giving: One of the most effective ways to minimize inheritance taxes is by making charitable gifts. You can choose to donate appreciated assets such as stocks, bonds, or real estate, or you can make a cash gift.

2. Bequests: Another effective strategy is to make bequests in your will. By leaving a specific dollar amount or a percentage of your estate to your heirs, you can reduce the size of your estate and avoid paying estate taxes. 3. Life Insurance: You can also use life insurance to minimize inheritance taxes. 4. Qualified Personal Residence Trusts (QPRTs): QPRTs are a type of trust that allows you to transfer your primary residence to your heirs while minimizing estate taxes. Under a QPRT, you transfer the ownership of your primary residence to your heirs for a set period of time, usually 10 years or less. At the end of the transfer period, the residence reverts back to you or your heirs, and you can deduct the value of the transfer from your estate.

5. Grantor Retained Annuity Trusts (GRATs): GRATs are another type of trust that can help minimize estate taxes. Under a GRAT, you transfer a portion of your estate to your heirs while retaining an annuity for your lifetime. At your death, the annuity goes to your heirs, and you can deduct the value of the transfer from your estate.

6. Dynasty Trusts: Dynasty trusts are a type of trust that can help you transfer your assets to your heirs for generations to come. These trusts can help you avoid estate taxes and provide your heirs with a tax-free inheritance.
